study.notes: STUDY: 24 week open label prospective randomised study in 176 overweight or obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (Rotterdam criteria; population recorded as obesity, PCOS noted), exenatide 10 ug twice daily (dose_mg 0.01 per injection) vs metformin 1000 mg twice daily for the first 12 weeks, then metformin alone in both arms (the randomised contrast is the 12 week one); registered ChiCTR-IIR-16008084; 158 completed the first 12 weeks (78 exenatide, 80 metformin; completers analysed, n per Table 2); Table 2 gives baseline and 12 week mean (SD) per arm (Results are presented as mean ± SD) with the interaction p of the repeated measures ANOVA (route arm_change_imputed_r, correlation 0.5, interaction p in the row notes); weight loss 4.29 ± 1.29 kg exenatide vs 2.28 ± 0.55 kg metformin (text, dispersion as printed), pct_weight_change -2.64 computed by the session: 100*(-4.29)/72.96 = -5.88 and 100*(-2.28)/70.38 = -3.24, corrected -2.64 percentage points; secondary outcomes prespecified (fat mass, insulin resistance, lipids, inflammatory marker); funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (industry_funded FALSE); first author from the record (Liu); rob_overall some_concerns

json.design: open label randomised trial, exenatide vs metformin for 12 weeks then metformin in both arms, 176 randomised, 158 completers at 12 weeks, overweight or obese women with PCOS
json.reason: population polycystic ovary syndrome with overweight or obesity, held under amendment A6 (Director decision on held populations); eight Table 2 rows extracted in full and kept in staging; first closed as extracted on 16 October and corrected to held the same day

rob.justification: S: randomised without a described method or concealment (D1); open label (D2); 18 of 176 did not complete the first 12 weeks, completers analysed (D3); laboratory and DXA outcomes (D4 low); registered, outcomes named in the methods (D5 low)

doubts: Table 2 dispersion is the SD per the Methods, while the weight figure uses SEM; the weight loss sentence's ± values are read as printed
PCOS population: overweight or obese women without diabetes, recorded as obesity
units printed as nmol/L for lipids are read as mmol/L
